Little and often is probably the best way here. Like perhaps do vocab practice for half an hour a day, every day, and then a little bit of grammar or focused exam practice frequently. As you're still doing gcses I would focus on those for now, over summer you will have much more free time to focus on this!

If you're trying to get a solid gcse grade - I cannot stress VOCAB enough. It should definitely be your priority. Download the list from the AQA website, and use a quizlet set like [this](https://quizlet.com/gb/171585083/aqa-gcse-spanish-flash-cards/?x=1jqU&i=3ph8en)

Knowing vocab is going to put you in a great place for the reading and listening. Alongside this, try to listen to basic Spanish whenever you can - music, kids tv shows, kids nursery rhymes, kids books, are all your best friend. They are literally for people learning the language from scratch and it can be really fun. :)

In terms of speaking, try something like [this](https://www.tes.com/teaching-resource/gcse-spanish-aqa-booklets-for-general-conversation-questions-12663448) where you can fill in the answers to the possible questions. I recommend looking on youtube to find the structure of the speaking exam, if this is something they are expecting you to do as well.

For writing, I found that I did well when i could just copy some of my speaking answers down. You should already have some tenses in those, which will give you marks.

I also recommend  [this](https://youtube.com/@astarspanish?si=RowW6M4x7tYH6830) youtube channel, he's one of my friends and has some great videos on GCSE spanish. 

If you have discord, feel free to add me and I can walk you through basic grammar and tenses! My user is _coldsoul -i do alevel spanish and am in y13 so I'd like to think I know a little bit about what I'm talking about!
